page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, the x86_64 architecture processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 38 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 219.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 54.69 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 262 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate that the server prioritizes memory capacity over raw compute speed. In CPU-bound tests, the instance recorded a stress-ng single-core score of 1035.08 and a multi-core score of 2724.76, placing it in the lower performance tiers. Similarly, Geekbench 5 testing yielded a single-core score of 885.0 and a multi-core score of 1970.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks showed a read-only small block cached speed of 151.25 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 17.19 GB/sec. For database and key-value operations, the server achieved 2.63 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, while static web serving throughput reached 3.0 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M8-4ms offers a specialized resource profile. It provides a massive memory footprint without requiring the acquisition of excess vCPUs, making it highly efficient for workloads constrained by RAM capacity rather than processing power. However, the tradeoff is relatively low compute performance per vCPU, as evidenced by its lower benchmark rankings. This server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale caching layers, in-memory databases, and enterprise workloads that demand substantial memory capacity but do not require high-performance parallel processing.
